subject: CleverHealth launch: quota bump & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Caroline Moss <caroline@cleverhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, ops@cleverhealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [CleverHealth] Launch next week — temporary quota bump request

Neha / Redwood ops team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We confirmed internal dry runs and are planning a staggered public launch on Mon 6/15. Based on our canary metrics, we expect a ~3x spike in inference requests during the first 48 hours (mainly short service calls, median prompt length ~75 tokens, peak concurrency ~220).

Can Redwood provision a temporary quota increase (tokens/min and concurrent requests) to handle the initial surge? We will provide a pre-signed traffic schedule but need a quick yes/no on what you can support and any constraints (model fallbacks, soft-throttles) so we can shape the rollout.

I attached an initial traffic estimate (surge-traffic-estimates.xlsx). Also looping in ops@cleverhealth.com for any infra coordination.

—Caroline
Caroline Moss
Head of Product Growth, CleverHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Moss <caroline@cleverhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [CleverHealth] Launch next week — temporary quota bump request

Team — forwarding Caroline's note and the attached estimates. Quick asks so we can respond to CleverHealth before EOD today: 

1) What exact quota increases are reasonable for a 48h surge given their numbers? Tokens/min + concurrent request caps.
2) Can we support an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant (and how would that affect latency/quality)?
3) Any required paperwork or SLA exceptions (temp-rate-exemption-form) to sign before we change quotas?
4) Ops: what monitoring/alerting should we enable for the 48h window (SLOs to watch, runbook)?

I've attached the customer's spreadsheet (surge-traffic-estimates.xlsx). Caroline, we'll propose a concrete plan once I hear back from infra and product — aim to confirm today.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Moss <caroline@cleverhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [CleverHealth] Launch next week — temporary quota bump request

Quick technical readout: given the numbers in the spreadsheet (median 75 tokens, peak concurrency ~220), we can support a temporary tokens/min increase and a higher concurrent request cap for a 48h window if we provision a short-lived dedicated pool or reserve burst capacity on hosted for their account. Notes: 

- Tokens/min: Recommend +2.5x default (safe headroom) as an initial offer. We can do +3x if they accept model-variant fallback.
- Concurrency: bump the per-customer concurrency cap to 300 for 48h; requires autoscale policy with a warmup window of ~10 mins.
- Fallback: define an ordered fallback: production model -> quantized variant (slightly lower quality) -> smaller architecture (fast). We can wire this into routing policy but need product to sign off on acceptable fallbacks.
- Monitoring: enable enhanced token-level tracing and a temporary dashboard (latency p50/p95, error rate, model fallback rate). Ops should set alerts at 5% error or >20% fallback rate.

I attached the temp-rate-exemption-form.docx for the legal/ops checklist. Ops will need the signed form before we flip quotas.

Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Moss <caroline@cleverhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [CleverHealth] Launch next week — temporary quota bump request

Thanks Rishi — product alignment items: 

- Fallback policy: approved in principle. We need customer sign-off on the mutual action plan that states fallback may reduce quality/latency tradeoffs during spikes (I can draft a short paragraph).
- Rollout suggestion: staggered ramp over 3 windows (0-6h low %, 6-24h medium %, 24-48h full) so we can verify real traffic patterns. That reduces risk of catastrophic surge.
- Roadmap note: this is not a long-term capacity increase; engineering will not change global defaults. If CleverHealth wants sustained higher throughput, we should discuss Dedicated pool options (sales/contract).

I'll pull together the mutual action plan and the fallback wording (will upload as cleverhealth_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf).

Lauren Bishop
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Moss <caroline@cleverhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: [CleverHealth] Launch next week — quota bump & mutual action plan (final)

Caroline — quick summary and next steps (finalized):

1) Temporary quota increase approved: tokens/min +2.5x for 48h, concurrency cap to 300. If you accept fallback behavior listed below we can consider +3x.
2) Fallback policy: production -> quantized variant -> smaller model. Lauren will share a one-paragraph consent clause; we need CleverHealth sign-off.
3) Rollout cadence: recommended stagger (0-6h, 6-24h, 24-48h) to surface real traffic. We will hold full-capacity flip until initial 6h window passes.
4) Paperwork: please sign the attached temp-rate-exemption-form.docx and return to ops@redwood.com. Ops (cc'd) will enable the temporary dashboard and alerts.
5) Timeline: if form is returned by EOD Friday (6/12), infra will provision and we will enable bump on Mon 6/15 08:00 PDT.

Attachments included: cleverhealth_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf, surge-traffic-estimates.xlsx, temp-rate-exemption-form.docx

Action owners: 
- Caroline/CleverHealth: sign temp-rate-exemption-form + confirm final traffic windows.
- Ops (Redwood): enable dashboard + alerts; stand up dedicated burst pool.
- Rishi: implement fallback routing and validate warmup.
- Lauren: upload mutual action plan paragraph for customer acceptance.

If everyone is aligned I will send a final signed MA plan and an Ops ticket to provision capacity.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
